quarterly_data.signal: Xcel Energy's second-quarter 2026 earnings release: SPS's October 2025 RFP solicited 870 MW of accredited capacity through 2032; the portfolio selection report was publicly filed with the NMPRC in July 2026 and project CCNs are expected to be filed in late 2026 or early 2027. SPS' preferred portfolio totals 3,928 MW of nameplate capacity, including 1,305 MW of PPAs (wind 305 MW and solar + storage 1,000 MW) alongside company-owned wind of 500 MW, company-owned solar of 1,890 MW and company-owned natural gas. From its July 2024 RFP, SPS is continuing to pursue approximately 2,800 MW of accredited resources, including approximately 4,000 MW of nameplate capacity company owned resources and approximately 500 MW of nameplate capacity PPAs.
quarterly_data.figure: SPS preferred portfolio 3,928 MW nameplate (PPAs 1,305 MW: wind 305 MW, solar + storage 1,000 MW; company-owned wind 500 MW, solar 1,890 MW); October 2025 RFP 870 MW accredited; July 2024 RFP ~2,800 MW accredited (~4,000 MW company owned nameplate, ~500 MW PPAs)

quarterly_data.signal: Xcel Energy's second-quarter 2026 earnings release: NSP-Minnesota and NSP-Wisconsin's December 2025 RFP seeks up to 3,500 MW of wind, solar, hydro, standalone storage or hybrid capacity that will achieve commercial operation by December 31, 2030; short-listed projects were announced in June 2026 and filing for regulatory approval is expected by the end of 2026. For PSCo, the CPUC in November 2025 approved a load forecast reflecting 3% compound annual sales growth through 2031 and a generation capacity need of approximately 5,400 MW; the Phase II RFP, expected to be issued in the third quarter of 2026, will seek the balance of resource needs through 2031 after consideration of 3,800 MW of approved acquisitions from the Near-Term Procurement RFP.
quarterly_data.figure: NSP System RFP up to 3,500 MW (commercial operation by December 31, 2030); PSCo approved load forecast of 3% compound annual sales growth through 2031 and generation capacity need of ~5,400 MW; 3,800 MW of approved Near-Term Procurement RFP acquisitions; Phase II RFP expected Q3 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Xcel Energy's second-quarter 2026 earnings release, in its note on NSP-Minnesota's electric service agreement to power a new Google data center in Minnesota (whose approval request includes a proposed Clean Energy Accelerator Charge for 1,900 MW of clean energy resources), states that approvals for 1,000 MW of resources for the Clean Energy Accelerator program are pending as part of existing resource acquisition processes, and that the remaining resources are expected to be requested in those processes by the end of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 1,000 MW of Clean Energy Accelerator program resources pending approval; remaining resources to be requested by end of 2026
